Imagine you have a circular piece of plywood. You randomly hammer 6 nails into the very edge of the circle. If you wrap a rubber band around those nails, what are the odds that the center of the wood is trapped inside that rubber band?

This is a pretty classic problem in the field of geometric probability. The idea was inspired by a video I saw online, but a detailed write-up can also be found at [Brainstellar](https://brainstellar.com/puzzles/211) (along with some other really interesting puzzles!)

## Interactive Simulation

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import { createInteractiveCircle } from "./visualization.js"

app = {
  // 1. Setup Layout with RAW HTML Inputs
  // We manually create the inputs so we control exactly how they sync
  const container = html`<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; font-family: sans-serif;">
    
    <div class="controls-container" style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 15px; margin-bottom: 20px;">
       
       <label style="font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px;">Points (n)</label>
       
       <input type="range" id="slider-input" min="3" max="12" step="1" value="6" style="width: 120px; cursor: pointer;">
       
       <input type="number" id="number-input" min="3" max="12" value="6" style="width: 50px; padding: 4px; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px;">
       
       <button class="randomize-btn" style="margin-left: 10px;">Randomize Positions</button>
    </div>

    <div id="canvas-container"></div>
  </div>`;

  // 2. Select Elements
  const rangeInput = container.querySelector("#slider-input");
  const numberInput = container.querySelector("#number-input");
  const randBtn = container.querySelector(".randomize-btn");
  const canvasContainer = container.querySelector("#canvas-container");

  // 3. State Variables
  let currentLogic = null; 
  let currentN = 6; // The source of truth for the last valid state
  
  // 4. Helper: Update Canvas
  function updateCanvas(n, mode) {
    if (currentLogic) currentLogic.dispose();
    
    canvasContainer.innerHTML = "";
    const c = DOM.canvas(400, 400);
    canvasContainer.appendChild(c);
    
    currentLogic = createInteractiveCircle(c, n, mode);
    currentN = n;
  }

  // 5. Validator
  function parseAndValidate(value) {
    const num = Number(value);
    if (isNaN(num) || !Number.isInteger(num)) return null; // No decimals
    if (num < 3 || num > 12) return null; // Strict bounds
    return num;
  }

  // 6. Event: SLIDER Input
  // The slider is constrained by HTML attributes, so it's always valid.
  rangeInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const val = rangeInput.valueAsNumber;
    
    // Update State
    currentN = val;
    
    // Sync Number Box
    numberInput.value = val;
    numberInput.style.border = "1px solid #ccc"; // Clear errors
    numberInput.style.outline = "none";
    
    // Update Visual
    updateCanvas(val, "even");
  });

  // 7. Event: NUMBER BOX Input
  numberInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const val = parseAndValidate(numberInput.value);
    
    if (val !== null) {
      // VALID: Sync slider and update visual
      numberInput.style.border = "1px solid #ccc";
      numberInput.style.outline = "none";
      
      rangeInput.value = val; // Move slider to match
      currentN = val;
      updateCanvas(val, "even");
    } else {
      // INVALID: Error style, BUT DO NOT TOUCH THE SLIDER
      numberInput.style.border = "2px solid red";
      numberInput.style.outline = "none";
      // The slider remains at 'currentN', preventing the "jump" effect
    }
  });

  // 8. Event: Blur (Cleanup)
  numberInput.addEventListener("blur", () => {
    const val = parseAndValidate(numberInput.value);
    if (val === null) {
      // If user leaves the box while it's invalid, revert to last truth
      numberInput.value = currentN;
      numberInput.style.border = "1px solid #ccc";
      numberInput.style.outline = "none";
    }
  });

  // 9. Event: Randomize
  randBtn.onclick = () => {
    if (currentLogic) currentLogic.randomize();
  };

  // 10. Start
  updateCanvas(6, "even");

  return container;
}
```

## The Mathematical Derivation

Instead of calculating the probability of the center being *inside*, we calculate the probability of the **complement**: the center being **outside**.

### 1. The Semicircle Condition

The center of the circle lies outside the polygon if and only if all points lie within the same arc (a semicircle).

### 2. Fixing a Boundary

## Results

| Points | Probability |
|--------|-------------|
| 3      | 25.0%       |
| 4      | 37.5%       |
| 5      | 50.0%       |
| 6      | 62.5%       |
| 10     | 87.9%       |

As $n \to \infty$, the probability approaches 1.

## Conclusion

This problem beautifully demonstrates how geometric intuition connects to discrete probability. The interactive visualization above lets you explore different values of $n$ and see the pattern emerge.
